meetDoctor.title: Dr. Adonis Maiquez, MD
meetDoctor.paragraph1: Dr. Adonis uses a functional medicine approach to identify the root causes of your medical issues, from cognitive decline, weight gain, hormone imbalance, chronic fatigue, to auto-immune or chronic degenerative diseases or if you want to assess and address risk factors for diseases that run in your family, or need medical support and follow-up after a health event such as a stroke or heart attack.
meetDoctor.paragraph2: Most health issues are multi-factorial, meaning it goes beyond genetics, encompassing life-style, environmental, metabolic pathways, vitamin, hormone and toxin levels. Many biochemical processes affect disease and aging, including oxidation, inflammation, detoxification and others. Addressing those variables together in a unified, individualized program supports prevention efforts, symptom management, and overall health. Dr. Adonis believes that we need a balance of our body, mind and spirit to accomplish a healthy and fulfilled life.
meetDoctor.paragraph3: Dr. Adonis is dual-certified in Functional Medicine and Anti-Aging Regenerative Medicine. brainProtocol.title: The Brain Protocol® — Alzheimer's & Cognitive Decline
brainProtocol.description:
SPECIALIZED CARE FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND MILD COGNITIVE DECLINE. Globally, hundreds of millions of people are affected by neurological disorders. In the United States, Alzheimer's disease alone affects an estimated 5.7 million individuals, and Mild Cognitive Decline — forgetfulness, language and thinking difficulties beyond normal aging — affects millions more.

The Brain Protocol® is Dr. Adonis's comprehensive, multivariable evaluation and care program, customized to each patient. It combines a complete medical history, laboratory testing, and an individualized plan addressing modifiable factors associated with cognitive health — such as cardiovascular risk, metabolic health, sleep, nutrition, and hormonal status — under ongoing medical supervision.

Treatment recommendations are individualized, and outcomes vary among patients. The Brain Protocol® is not represented as a treatment to cure or prevent Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, or other neurodegenerative conditions. Book an appointment to find out whether this evaluation is appropriate for you.

painManagement.title: Pain Management
painManagement.description:
Pain is a complex process and Neurosciences approach pain management from different angles. To be effective, pain management must address the entire loop — starting at the originating site (joint, spine, muscle, tendon) and addressing the nerves that bring signals to the brain.

We specialize in: joint and spine steroid and PRP (platelet-rich plasma) injections; nerve and plexus blocks; radiofrequency ablations. Dr. Adonis, trained as a neurosurgeon, is a member of the American Academy of Pain Management and the World Institute of Pain.

We evaluate and treat pain from car accidents, sport injuries, slips and falls, and chronic conditions such as osteoarthritis and inflammatory arthritis. Treatment plans are individualized, and outcomes vary among patients.

functionalMedicine.title: Functional Medicine
functionalMedicine.description:
Functional medicine follows an approach fairly different from conventional medicinal practices. This type of medicine recognizes each individual as being unique and, therefore, disproves the theory of offering standard solutions in targeting health conditions.

Dr. Adonis, a firm believer in functional medicine, is a member of the Institute for Functional Medicine — the most prestigious and recognized organization in the country. He has empowered thousands of patients to take ownership of their health and start their journey to wellness.

If a meaningful and healthy life with better understanding of your body and mind is your calling — get in touch with our clinic today.

executivePhysical.title: Executive Physical Program
executivePhysical.description:
To live a long, fruitful life we need to take care of our health. Being healthy means not just being disease-free but having mental, physical, and emotional well-being. Constant stress, faulty eating habits, and unhealthy lifestyles have brought deterioration in overall health.

The Executive Physical Program helps you get a clear picture of your current health status and begin your journey to a healthier you.

weightLoss.title: Medical Weight Management
weightLoss.description:
Our physician-led weight management program begins with a comprehensive medical evaluation — in person or virtual — including your medical history, habits, and laboratory analysis.

Based on that evaluation, Dr. Adonis designs an individualized plan that may include nutritional guidance, personalized physical activity, behavioral strategies and, only when medically appropriate, prescription treatment with ongoing medical monitoring.

Completing an evaluation does not guarantee that medication will be prescribed. Treatment decisions are made by the treating physician based on each patient's individual clinical circumstances.

hormoneTherapy.title: Bio-Identical Hormone Therapy
hormoneTherapy.description:
Think hormonal changes are just a woman's concern? Think again. Menopause in women and its counterpart — andropause or late-onset hypogonadism in men — are natural stages of life that can significantly affect your well-being.

Dr. Adonis, a renowned functional medicine specialist in Miami, FL, is here to guide you seamlessly through these transitions. His experience in bio-identical hormone therapy offers a comprehensive, individualized approach. Like all prescription therapies, hormone treatment has potential benefits, risks, contraindications, and adverse effects, and is appropriate only for selected patients after medical evaluation.

Personalized in-person consultations are available in Miami, and telemedicine consultations are available to eligible patients physically located in Florida.

menopauseAndropause.title: Menopause and Andropause
menopauseAndropause.description:
Dr. Adonis believes that menopause and andropause are phases that can be experienced with fulfillment and dignity. The experience varies from person to person depending on hereditary factors, constitution, and lifestyle.

Dr. A advocates an individualized approach that factors in all variables and suggests simple, sustainable measures to equip the body to manage these transitions with minimal medical intervention.

If you are looking to navigate andropause and menopause with an individualized plan and without unnecessary medication — book an appointment today.

agingBiomarkers.title: Aging Biomarkers
agingBiomarkers.description:
Dr. A has helped thousands of patients embrace aging with a positive outlook and alternative therapies. By minimizing dependency on medication, he equips patients to gain better control over their lives and habits, providing an environment more conducive to coping with aging.

If you are looking to add life to your years — book an appointment with our clinic.

autoimmune.title: Autoimmune Diseases
autoimmune.description:
Complex as they may be, autoimmune diseases can be diagnosed using a functional medicine protocol to arrive at the root cause. A complete study of hormones, vitamins, metabolic processes, inflammation, intestinal health, and other markers offers an in-depth view of the immune system.

Dr. Adonis has designed a multipronged approach for managing autoimmune diseases, enabling a near-normal and gratifying life. Conditions covered include thyroid disorders and various forms of arthritis.

fibromyalgia.title: Fibromyalgia / Chronic Fatigue
fibromyalgia.description:
An increasingly common ailment, over 3% of the US population suffers from fibromyalgia. Although it can occur in almost anyone, women seem to be more prone to it. Fibromyalgia is marked by widespread pain throughout the body without any clearly identifiable cause.

Dr. Adonis has extensive experience treating patients with FMS. Through years of study and practice, he uses a sustainable combination of techniques to help patients manage symptoms and improve quality of life. Treatment plans are individualized, and outcomes vary among patients.

brainHealth.title: Brain Health & Cognitive Wellness
brainHealth.description:
FOCUSED ON BRAIN HEALTH AND COGNITIVE WELLNESS. Brain health is one of the most important factors for overall well-being and quality of life. A healthy brain is responsible for optimal physiological functioning and cognitive processes — memory, language, focus, decision-making.

Dr. Adonis, trained as a neurosurgeon, uses his extensive practice of functional medicine to help patients understand the relationship between neurological processes and aging. He uses a multifunctional approach for those at risk of or suffering from Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Mild Cognitive Decline, and other neurodegenerative conditions.

Treatment recommendations are individualized, and outcomes vary among patients. Early evaluation allows more options to be considered — book your assessment today.

neurotransmitters.title: Brain Neurotransmitters
neurotransmitters.description:
Neurotransmitters are chemicals in the brain that send signals to the nerves. These signal molecules are responsible for several functions including learning, energy, and psychological states. An imbalance can have serious consequences for the body.

Dr. Adonis, trained as a neurosurgeon, combines neuroscience with functional medicine to evaluate factors that may affect neurotransmitter balance. Treatment recommendations are individualized, and outcomes vary among patients.

intestinalHealth.title: Intestinal Health
intestinalHealth.description:
Just as the brain controls voluntary and involuntary movement, the intestine looks after the immunity of the body. Good intestinal health helps with overall health.

Dr. Adonis employs the principles of functional medicine to improve gut health. A healthy intestine is not just the result of good genes, but the product of great care. Follow your gut and take time for yourself.

telomeres.title: Telomeres
telomeres.description:
Telomeres are the protective caps at the ends of chromosomes and an active area of aging research. Telomere length has population-level associations with aspects of aging, but it is not a standalone clinical measurement of biological age or individual lifespan.

Dr. Adonis helps patients understand the aging process and the factors they can act on — nutrition, physical activity, sleep, and metabolic health — as part of an individualized medical evaluation. When testing is appropriate, results are interpreted in clinical context; they do not predict lifespan or guarantee outcomes.

sexualHealth.title: Sexual Health
sexualHealth.description:
Sexual vitality is an important component of overall well-being. Hormonal factors can contribute to sexual symptoms in some patients. When clinically indicated, evaluation may include hormone testing and discussion of appropriate treatment options, for both men and women.

Care is individualized following medical evaluation, and outcomes vary among patients. Treatment is provided only when medically appropriate following evaluation by a licensed healthcare professional.

regenerativeExosomes.title: Exosomes from stem cells
regenerativeExosomes.description:
The Future of Healing Without Surgery

Regenerative medicine has taken a quantum leap in 2026. It's no longer just about alleviating symptoms, but about giving precise instructions to our cells so they can repair themselves. In this scenario, exosomes have become key players.

What are they and how do they work?
Exosomes are small vesicles that act as intelligent "messengers." They transport proteins, lipids, and genetic material from one cell to another. In regenerative medicine, they are being studied and used investigationally to:

  • Reduce systemic inflammation: They send signals that calm the exaggerated inflammatory response.
  • Accelerate tissue recovery: Ideal for patients with joint injuries or muscle atrophy.
  • Biological rejuvenation: They activate regeneration pathways that slow down with age.

The Role of Supplementation in Regeneration
For regenerative therapies to work, the body must have the necessary "raw materials." Therefore, the following are vital in this process:

  • Bioactive Peptides: These act as building blocks for new tissues.
  • Collagen and Elastin Inducers: These are essential for maintaining the architecture of the extracellular matrix.
  • Network Antioxidants: Such as glutathione, which protect new cells from oxidative stress during their formation.

Regulatory status: Exosome products are not FDA-approved to treat, cure, or prevent any disease, and their clinical use remains investigational. Whether any regenerative option is appropriate for a patient is determined by the treating clinician following medical evaluation.

peptideTherapy.title: Peptide Therapy Protocols
peptideTherapy.description:
Physician-supervised cellular optimization, GH secretagogues, tissue repair, and longevity peptides tailored to your biological needs.

Peptides are short chains of amino acids that serve as vital signaling molecules throughout your body. Our protocols utilize comprehensive diagnostic laboratory panels and FDA-compliant clinical sourcing to deliver targeted therapies for injury recovery, immune support, cognitive performance, and vitality.

Every protocol is individualized under medical supervision, with continuous monitoring and outcome tracking.

trt.title: Testosterone Replacement Therapy (TRT)
trt.description:
Comprehensive male hormonal evaluation and physician-supervised testosterone optimization protocols designed to address the root causes of fatigue, loss of muscle mass, decreased libido, and brain fog.

Rather than relying on a single total testosterone number, Dr. Adonis evaluates full biomarker panels including Free Testosterone, SHBG, Estradiol, and Hematocrit. We create individualized, precision-dosed protocols with regular follow-up and monitoring to restore peak vitality and long-term health.

enclomiphene.title: Enclomiphene Therapy
enclomiphene.description:
An advanced oral selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) protocol that stimulates your body's natural testosterone production while fully preserving testicular function and fertility.

By targeting estrogen receptors at the hypothalamus, enclomiphene prompts the pituitary to increase LH and FSH output, signaling your testes to produce endogenous testosterone naturally without exogenous suppression. Comprehensive hormone testing and ongoing monitoring ensure optimal physiological balance.

thyroid.title: Comprehensive Thyroid Optimization
thyroid.description:
In-depth functional thyroid evaluations that look far beyond standard TSH tests to uncover root causes of stubborn weight gain, chronic fatigue, brain fog, and temperature dysregulation.

Dr. Adonis tests complete thyroid panels—including Free T3, Free T4, Reverse T3, and thyroid antibodies (TPO and TgAb)—alongside gut health and nutritional cofactors. Treatment focuses on cellular conversion and customized endocrine support to restore metabolic vitality.

hashimotos.title: Hashimoto’s Autoimmune Thyroiditis
hashimotos.description:
Targeted functional medicine and immune-modulating care for Hashimoto’s thyroiditis, the leading cause of hypothyroidism in the United States.

Because the immune system is attacking the thyroid gland, optimal care requires addressing the immune dysfunction, intestinal permeability (leaky gut), nutrient deficiencies, and environmental triggers—not just prescribing standard synthetic hormone. Dr. Adonis designs comprehensive protocols to calm autoimmunity and protect thyroid tissue.

Our groundbreaking program offers a personalized pathway to gut health that harmonizes the latest scientific research with individualized care. We craft a plan that nurtures your gut health and empowers your body's natural healing abilities — through dietary guidance, targeted supplementation (probiotics, prebiotics, fiber), lifestyle adjustments, and hormone balance support when necessary.

gutHealthPage.lead: Bloating is not a personality trait. Neither is knowing where every bathroom is. There is usually a mechanism, and it is usually findable.

intro.title: What Gut Health Means
intro.lead: Most digestive complaints get one of two responses: a medication that reduces the symptom, or a workup that finds nothing structural and concludes the problem is stress. Both leave the patient managing something indefinitely.
intro.p2: Your digestive tract does considerably more than digest. It houses the majority of your immune tissue, manufactures neurotransmitters including a large share of your body’s serotonin, absorbs every nutrient you depend on, and maintains a barrier separating your bloodstream from everything you swallow.
intro.callout: There is usually a mechanism, and it is usually findable.
intro.p4: When that system falters, the effects reach well past digestion. Fatigue, brain fog, mood changes, skin problems, joint pain, hormone symptoms, and autoimmune activity all trace back to the gut in a meaningful number of patients.

immune.title: Immune Headquarters
immune.desc: The majority of your immune tissue lives in the digestive tract, which is why gut dysfunction shows up as inflammation elsewhere.

neuro.title: Neurotransmitter Production
neuro.desc: A large share of your body’s serotonin is manufactured in the gut, which is why mood and brain fog so often track with digestion.

nutrients.title: Nutrient Absorption
nutrients.desc: Every nutrient you depend on is absorbed here. Malabsorption creates deficiencies no amount of diet quality can correct.

catalog.title: The Dysfunctions We Most Often Find
catalog.subtitle: Comprehensive testing usually explains in one round what years of elimination diets could not.

d1.name: Dysbiosis
d1.description: The bacterial population has shifted. Beneficial species are reduced, less helpful ones have expanded. This affects digestion, immune signaling, and inflammation.

d2.name: SIBO
d2.description: Bacteria that belong in the large intestine have colonized the small intestine, where they ferment food before you absorb it. Classic presentation is bloating that worsens through the day and reacts to fiber and healthy foods.

d3.name: Increased Intestinal Permeability
d3.description: The barrier has loosened, allowing partially digested proteins and bacterial components into circulation, where they provoke immune responses. Implicated across autoimmune and inflammatory conditions.

d4.name: Low Stomach Acid or Enzyme Insufficiency
d4.description: Food is not being broken down adequately, which causes reflux more often than people expect and leaves nutrients unabsorbed.

d5.name: Food Sensitivities
d5.description: Immune reactivity to specific foods, distinct from allergy, often delayed by hours or days and therefore difficult to identify without testing.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.subtitle: Order matters in gut work. We test first, then correct in sequence.

p1.title: We Test Rather Than Guess
p1.description: Elimination diets by trial and error can take months and often end with a patient eating fifteen foods and still feeling unwell. Comprehensive stool analysis, permeability markers, SIBO breath testing where indicated, and food sensitivity panels shorten that enormously.

p2.title: We Follow A Sequence
p2.description: Order matters in gut work. Remove what should not be there, replace what digestion requires, restore the bacterial population, and repair the lining. Introducing probiotics into an untreated overgrowth frequently makes patients feel worse, which is why sequence is not a detail.

p3.title: We Connect The Gut To Your Other Symptoms
p3.description: Patients frequently arrive for bloating and mention almost as an afterthought that they are exhausted, foggy, and their skin has been bad for two years. Those are often the same problem. Malabsorption produces nutrient deficiency. Permeability produces systemic inflammation. Dysbiosis affects neurotransmitter production.

p4.title: We Rule Out What Needs Ruling Out
p4.description: Blood in the stool, unintentional weight loss, difficulty swallowing, persistent vomiting, or a family history of colon cancer means gastroenterology and appropriate imaging or endoscopy. We refer rather than work around it.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about digestive testing, treatment, and what to expect.

f1.q: My colonoscopy was normal. Why do I still have symptoms?
f1.a: A colonoscopy looks for structural disease — inflammation, ulceration, growths. It is excellent at that and it does not assess your microbiome, enzyme output, barrier integrity, or food reactivity. A normal result rules out serious pathology. It does not explain your symptoms.

f2.a: IBS describes a pattern of symptoms after other causes are excluded. It names what you are experiencing rather than why. In our experience a meaningful proportion of IBS patients have identifiable dysbiosis, SIBO, or food sensitivity underneath the label.

f3.q: Should I just take a probiotic?
f3.a: Not before testing. Probiotics help in some situations and worsen others, particularly with untreated small intestinal overgrowth. Sequence and strain selection matter more than most people are told.

f4.q: How long do I need to avoid foods?
f4.a: Elimination is usually a defined phase, not a permanent state. The aim is to reduce reactivity, repair the lining, and reintroduce systematically. Many patients get most of their diet back.

f5.q: Is leaky gut a real thing?
f5.a: Increased intestinal permeability is a measurable, well-documented physiological phenomenon studied across a range of inflammatory and autoimmune conditions. The popular term is loose. The mechanism is real and testable.

f6.q: How long until I feel better?
f6.a: Most patients report meaningful change within 90 days. Some symptoms move within weeks; microbiome and lining restoration take longer.

f7.a: No. This is a cash-pay practice and we do not provide superbills. Your labs and consultations are included in your program.

brainHealthPage.title: Brain Health in Miami, FL
brainHealthPage.lead: You walk into a room and cannot recall why. A word you have used your whole life sits just out of reach. This gets attributed to age, stress, or having a lot on. Often it is not, and the alternative explanations are measurable.

intro.title: What Brain Health Means Here
intro.lead: Your brain is metabolically expensive. It represents roughly two percent of body weight and consumes about twenty percent of your energy.
intro.p2: That demand makes it unusually sensitive to anything affecting fuel supply, inflammation, or hormonal signaling. Which is why cognitive symptoms so often arrive as the first visible sign of a problem somewhere else entirely.
intro.callout: Being told it is stress is not a workup.
intro.p4: Reading takes twice as long because you keep going back. Names sit just out of reach. Sometimes age and stress are the correct explanation — and often they are not, which is exactly why the question is worth testing rather than assuming.

catalog.title: The Drivers We Most Commonly Find
catalog.subtitle: Cognitive symptoms have causes, and most of the common ones show up on a comprehensive panel.

d1.name: Metabolic
d1.description: Insulin resistance impairs the brain’s ability to use glucose. The relationship between glycemic dysfunction and cognitive decline is well documented, and it is frequently present years before a diabetes diagnosis.

d2.name: Vascular
d2.description: The brain depends on dense small-vessel circulation. Blood pressure, lipids, and endothelial function determine how well that circulation delivers.

d3.name: Hormonal
d3.description: Thyroid hormone directly regulates neuronal metabolism. Estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone all have receptors in the brain, and cognitive complaints appearing during perimenopause or andropause are frequently hormonal rather than psychological.

d4.name: Inflammatory
d4.description: Systemic inflammation crosses into the central nervous system. Autoimmune activity, chronic infection, and gut permeability all contribute.

d5.name: Nutritional
d5.description: B12, folate, vitamin D, omega-3s, magnesium, and iron are each required for neurological function, and deficiency is common and correctable.

d6.name: Sleep
d6.description: Clearance of metabolic waste from the brain occurs predominantly during sleep. Untreated sleep apnea is one of the most consequential and most missed contributors to cognitive decline.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.subtitle: We treat cognitive symptoms as a finding to be worked up, not a phase to be waited out.

p1.title: We Treat Cognitive Symptoms As A Finding, Not A Phase
p1.description: Brain fog in a 45-year-old is frequently waved off. It should be worked up, because the causes underneath it are largely correctable and because the same drivers left running for two decades are the ones associated with long-term cognitive decline.

p2.title: We Test Broadly
p2.description: Your panel may include fasting glucose, insulin and HbA1c, a complete lipid panel, inflammatory markers including hs-CRP and homocysteine, complete thyroid function, sex and adrenal hormones, B12, folate, vitamin D, magnesium, iron and ferritin, autoimmune antibodies, heavy metals, and chronic infection markers.

p3.title: We Take Sleep Seriously
p3.description: If your history suggests obstructive sleep apnea — snoring, witnessed pauses, unrefreshing sleep, morning headache — we pursue that before anything else. It is common, treatable, and one of the highest-yield findings in cognitive medicine.

p4.title: We Refer When Referral Is Right
p4.description: Rapidly progressing memory loss, personality change, difficulty with familiar tasks, disorientation to time or place, or new neurological symptoms require neurological evaluation and imaging. We will say so directly rather than starting a supplement protocol.

p5.title: We Work On The Long Horizon Too
p5.description: The metabolic, vascular, and inflammatory factors that produce brain fog now are the same ones associated with cognitive decline decades later. Correcting them addresses both.

intro.lead: An autoimmune condition is one in which the immune system fails to distinguish your tissue from a threat, and attacks it. There are more than eighty recognized conditions, and which one you have depends mostly on which tissue is targeted.
intro.p2: Thyroid, and you have Hashimoto’s or Graves’. Joints, rheumatoid arthritis. Intestinal lining, celiac or Crohn’s. Skin, psoriasis. Nervous system, multiple sclerosis. Connective tissue, lupus.
intro.callout: They are treated as separate diseases by separate specialists. The underlying mechanism is the same.
intro.p4: Autoimmune conditions also cluster. Once you have one, your risk of a second is meaningfully elevated. Patients often accumulate diagnoses over a decade, each treated in isolation by a different specialist, when what is actually happening is one immune system behaving one way.

catalog.title: The Three Components
catalog.subtitle: Two of these three can be addressed. That is the entire basis of this approach.

d1.name: Genetic Susceptibility
d1.description: Your inherited risk determines which tissue is vulnerable and how readily tolerance is lost. This is the one component of the three that cannot be changed, which is precisely why the other two matter so much.

d2.name: An Environmental Trigger
d2.description: Infection, toxin, chronic stress, or dietary antigen. Something set the immune activity in motion, and identifying it is the question conventional care most often sets aside in favor of suppressing the attack.

d3.name: Increased Intestinal Permeability
d3.description: A loosened intestinal barrier appears across a wide range of autoimmune conditions. Proteins that should stay inside the gut reach the bloodstream and provoke immune responses, which is one proposed route to loss of tolerance.

approach.title: Our Approach

catalog.title: Three Patterns Worth Knowing

d1.name: Antibodies Come First
d1.description: Antibodies frequently appear years, sometimes a decade, before thyroid hormone levels drop far enough to trigger a diagnosis. During that window patients feel unwell, get tested, and are told their thyroid is fine, because nobody ordered antibodies.

d2.name: The Swing Pattern
d2.description: As the gland is damaged, stored hormone is released in bursts, so patients cycle between hyperthyroid-feeling periods of anxiety and racing heart and hypothyroid-feeling periods of exhaustion. That instability is often misread as anxiety or a mood disorder.

d3.name: Genetics, Trigger, Permeability

f2.q: Why does my doctor not test antibodies?
f2.a: Because in conventional practice the result often would not change the treatment. If the plan is hormone replacement either way, the antibody result is informational. In our approach it changes the plan entirely, so we order it.

f3.q: Do I have to go gluten-free?

f4.q: Will I still need thyroid medication?
f4.a: Probably, and possibly permanently. Damaged thyroid tissue does not come back. What root-cause treatment aims to change is how much further damage occurs and how well you feel on your dose.

f5.q: My antibodies are high but my thyroid levels are normal. Is that a problem?
f5.a: It is an early finding worth acting on. Elevated antibodies with normal hormone levels means the immune attack is underway and the gland is still compensating. This is the most useful moment to intervene.

thyroidPage.lead: Your thyroid is not one number. It is a chain that can break in four different places, and three of them are invisible on the test most people are given.

intro.title: What Thyroid Dysfunction Is
intro.lead: The thyroid produces hormones that set the metabolic rate of nearly every cell you have. When output falls, everything slows. When it rises, everything accelerates.
intro.p2: The chain matters because most thyroid problems are not the gland failing. Your thyroid mainly produces T4, which is largely inactive. T4 has to convert into T3, the form your cells actually use, and that conversion happens outside the thyroid, in the liver, kidneys, and gut.
intro.callout: A person can have a normal TSH, adequate T4, and still be functionally hypothyroid. That patient will be told nothing is wrong.

hypo.title: Hypothyroidism
hypo.desc: Underproduction. Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, hair loss, brain fog, low mood, and slow recovery. By far the more common presentation.

hyper.title: Hyperthyroidism
hyper.desc: Overproduction. Anxiety, racing heart, weight loss, heat intolerance, tremor, and insomnia.

sub.title: Subclinical Dysfunction
sub.desc: Where most of our patients sit. TSH is drifting but has not crossed the threshold, or looks acceptable while the hormones downstream do not. Symptoms are present. Treatment has not been offered.

catalog.title: Where The Chain Breaks
catalog.subtitle: A signal from the pituitary, a hormone produced by the gland, a conversion step in the liver and gut, and receptors that have to receive it.

d1.name: The Signal
d1.description: TSH is a pituitary hormone. It measures the signal being sent, not the hormone being produced, converted, or received. Testing TSH alone to assess thyroid function is like judging a delivery by checking whether the order was placed.

d2.name: Production
d2.description: Your thyroid mainly produces T4, which is largely inactive. Autoimmune attack is the most common reason production falls, and antibodies frequently show up years before hormone levels move.

d3.name: Conversion
d3.category: Liver, Kidneys & Gut — T4 to T3
d3.description: T4 has to convert into T3, the form your cells actually use, and that happens outside the thyroid. Under chronic stress, inflammation, nutrient deficiency, or illness, the body converts T4 into reverse T3 instead.

d4.name: Reception
d4.description: Reverse T3 occupies the receptor without activating it. A person can have a normal TSH, adequate T4, and still be functionally hypothyroid. That patient will be told nothing is wrong.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.subtitle: Testing TSH alone to assess thyroid function is like judging a delivery by checking whether the order was placed.
approach.quote: “Being healthy is more than the absence of visible disease. There is a great deal happening inside the body that needs to be addressed long before it becomes a disorder.”

p1.title: We Run The Full Panel, Not TSH
p1.description: Your panel may include TSH, free T4, free T3, reverse T3, thyroid peroxidase antibodies, thyroglobulin antibodies, ferritin, iron, vitamin D, B12, selenium, zinc, and inflammatory markers. Labs can be completed in our office, or locally at any Quest or LabCorp.

p2.title: We Check Antibodies On Every Patient
p2.description: The most common cause of hypothyroidism is autoimmune, and antibodies frequently show up years before thyroid hormone levels move. Finding them early changes the entire treatment plan, because the problem is then an immune system attacking the gland rather than a gland that quit.

p3.title: We Read Optimal, Not Just Normal
p3.description: Reference ranges describe the population that walked into the lab, which includes a great many people with undiagnosed thyroid disease. A free T3 at the bottom edge of range, next to elevated reverse T3 and low ferritin, tells a story that no single value tells alone.

p4.title: We Treat The Reason It Broke
p4.description: Low ferritin impairs conversion. So does low selenium and zinc, chronic cortisol elevation, gut inflammation, and insulin resistance. Prescribing thyroid hormone while those remain uncorrected means chasing dose increases that never quite work.

f1.q: My TSH is normal. Can I still have a thyroid problem?

f2.q: What is reverse T3 and why does it matter?
f2.a: Reverse T3 is an inactive form your body produces from T4 under stress, illness, inflammation, or nutrient deficiency. It binds thyroid receptors without activating them. f3.q: I’m already on levothyroxine and still feel terrible. Why?

intro.title: What Fibromyalgia Is
intro.lead: You have probably been told the tests were normal. You may have been told it was stress, or depression, or that you should try to relax.
intro.p2: Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and cognitive difficulty. The current understanding centers on central sensitization: the nervous system’s pain processing has become amplified, so signals that should register as mild register as severe, and stimuli that should not register as painful do.
intro.callout: This is not imagination and it is not a low pain threshold. It is a change in how the central nervous system processes input.
intro.p4: The problem is that the standard workup was never designed to find what drives it, so the absence of findings gets interpreted as the absence of a problem.

intro.title: What Enclomiphene Is
intro.lead: Enclomiphene is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that increases your body’s own testosterone production.
intro.p2: The mechanism is upstream. Your hypothalamus and pituitary monitor circulating estrogen as a proxy for how much testosterone is around. When they detect enough, they reduce LH and FSH output, and the testicles produce less. Enclomiphene blocks estrogen receptors at the hypothalamus, so the brain reads the level as low and increases LH and FSH.
intro.callout: The outcome is a higher testosterone level generated by your own physiology, with the pituitary-testicular axis intact and sperm production preserved.
intro.p4: Enclomiphene is the isomer of clomiphene citrate responsible for the testosterone-raising effect, separated out from the isomer associated with more of the estrogenic side effects.
intro.scopeNote: Important context: enclomiphene is prescribed off-label for male hypogonadism and is dispensed as a compounded medication. We say this plainly because you should know what you are taking. Off-label prescribing is legal, common, and physician-directed, and it means the FDA has not approved this specific indication.

f1.q: Is ED a sign of heart disease?
f1.a: It can be an early one. The arteries supplying erectile tissue are narrower than the coronary arteries, so endothelial dysfunction often shows there first. That is why our workup includes cardiovascular and metabolic markers rather than hormones alone.

f2.q: Can’t I just get a prescription online?
f2.a: You can. What you will not get is an explanation. If your ED is driven by low testosterone, insulin resistance, or early vascular disease, a PDE5 inhibitor manages the evening and leaves the cause running.

f3.q: Will testosterone therapy fix my ED?
f3.a: It helps when low testosterone is a contributor, particularly for libido. But testosterone alone does not resolve ED with a primarily vascular cause. Testing tells us which you are dealing with.

f7.q: Does ED medication have side effects?
f7.a: PDE5 inhibitors commonly cause headache, flushing, nasal congestion, and indigestion. They are absolutely contraindicated with nitrates. We review your medications and cardiac history before prescribing anything.

f8.q: I’m in my thirties. Is this normal?
f8.a: ED in younger men is more common than most assume and more likely to have an identifiable, correctable cause — metabolic, hormonal, medication-related, or psychological. It is worth investigating rather than waiting out.

intro.title: What Hormone Replacement Therapy Is
intro.lead: Hormone replacement therapy restores hormones your body has stopped producing at the levels it needs.
intro.p1: We use bioidentical hormones, meaning the molecules are structurally identical to the hormones your body makes. Estradiol given as HRT is the same estradiol your ovaries produced.
intro.callout: Identical structure means the hormone binds the same receptors and follows the same metabolic pathways as your own.
intro.p2: That is different from older synthetic formulations, which were structurally altered compounds that behaved differently in the body and carried a different side effect profile.

transitions.title: The Transitions HRT Is Used Across
transitions.subtitle: Hormone decline is not one event with one timeline, and the protocol differs with each.

t1.name: Perimenopause
t1.desc: The years before periods stop, often starting in the early to mid-forties. Hormones fluctuate rather than simply decline, which is why symptoms can be erratic and easy to dismiss.

t2.name: Menopause
t2.desc: Estrogen and progesterone drop substantially and stay down. Effects reach well past hot flashes into bone density, cardiovascular health, cognition, and sleep architecture.

t3.name: Andropause
t3.desc: Slower and less discussed. Testosterone declines gradually from roughly the mid-thirties.

t4.name: Clinical Deficiency At Any Age
t4.desc: Thyroid, adrenal, and sex hormone deficiencies occur in people nowhere near menopause. They are frequently missed because nobody tested for them.

hero.lead: Testosterone does not fall off a cliff. It erodes. Most men are handed a single total testosterone number and told it is within range. That number, on its own, explains almost nothing.

intro.title: What TRT Is
intro.lead: Testosterone replacement therapy restores testosterone to a healthy physiological range in men whose own production has declined.
intro.p1: Testosterone regulates far more than libido. It drives muscle protein synthesis, bone density, red blood cell production, fat distribution, insulin sensitivity, mood regulation, and cognition. When it falls, the effects are systemic, which is why the symptom list looks scattered until you understand the mechanism.
intro.callout: Levels decline gradually from roughly the mid-thirties. That decline is normal in the statistical sense. It is not automatically acceptable.
intro.p2: The workout that used to take a day to recover from now takes three. The afternoon you used to push through, you no longer push through. Drive went missing at some point and you cannot name the month it happened.

f1.title: Free, Not Just Total
f1.desc: Most testosterone in your blood is bound to SHBG and albumin and is not biologically available.

f2.title: Drawn In The Morning
f2.desc: Testosterone peaks early. Afternoon draws are one of the most common reasons men are wrongly told they are fine.

f3.title: Systemic Effects
f3.desc: Muscle, bone, red blood cells, fat distribution, insulin sensitivity, mood, and cognition all depend on it.

types.title: Primary or Secondary?
types.subtitle: They look identical from the outside and require different treatment. Distinguishing them requires LH and FSH, which a basic testosterone test does not include.

t1.name: Primary Hypogonadism
t1.desc: The testicles are not producing adequately. The signal from above is arriving, but the response to it is inadequate, so raising the signal alone will not fix the problem.

t2.name: Secondary Hypogonadism
t2.desc: The signal from the pituitary and hypothalamus has weakened, so the testicles are not being told to produce. If fertility matters to you, this distinction is the whole conversation, because restoring the signal is an option here.

approach.title: Our Approach
approach.subtitle: This is the difference between a subscription and a diagnosis.

p1.title: Full Panel, Not A Single Number
p1.desc: Total testosterone is the least informative number in male hormone medicine when read alone. Most testosterone in your blood is bound to SHBG and albumin and is not biologically available. Two men with identical total testosterone can have very different free testosterone, and only one of them feels it.

p2.title: We Look For Why It Dropped Before We Replace It
p2.desc: Low testosterone is frequently downstream of something else. Poor sleep, visceral fat driving aromatization, insulin resistance, chronic stress suppressing the pituitary signal, undiagnosed thyroid dysfunction, or nutrient deficiency. Replacing testosterone without addressing those leaves the cause running. This is the difference between a subscription and a diagnosis.

p3.title: Estradiol Is Managed, Not Ignored
p3.desc: Testosterone aromatizes into estradiol. Men need estradiol — it is protective for bone, cardiovascular health, and libido. Too much causes real problems. Clinics that never check it are managing half the equation, and clinics that reflexively suppress it create a different set of symptoms. We test it and treat what we find.

p4.title: Monitoring Is Part Of The Treatment, Not An Upsell
p4.desc: Hematocrit, PSA, estradiol, and lipids are checked on schedule for as long as you are on therapy. This is standard of care and it is not optional here.

f1.a: Semaglutide and tirzepatide are FDA-approved medications with extensive clinical trial data. BPC-157, TB-500, CJC-1295, and MOTS-c are not FDA-approved drugs. In July 2026, an FDA advisory committee voted to recommend three of them for pharmacy compounding eligibility, but that vote is non-binding and formal agency rulemaking remains pending. We review the precise regulatory status of every compound with you.

f2.q: What does the July 2026 FDA advisory vote actually change?
f2.a: On its own, nothing immediately. An advisory committee recommendation is expert counsel to the FDA, not a finalized regulation. The agency must still formally accept the recommendation and complete administrative rulemaking before compounding pharmacies have clear statutory authority. We track this closely to ensure compliance.

f3.a: Safety varies significantly depending on the specific peptide, dose, purity, and individual patient biology. Some peptides possess extensive human safety profiles, while others rely primarily on preclinical data. We discuss verified safety profiles, contraindications, and conduct required monitoring labs every 6 months.

f4.q: Can I buy peptides online instead?
f4.a: Products sold online marked "for research purposes only" or "not for human consumption" are not manufactured under pharmaceutical CGMP standards. Contamination, endotoxins, degraded chains, and inaccurate dosing are widespread risks. We strongly advise against unmonitored online sourcing.

f5.a: Most peptides are administered via subcutaneous micro-injections using an ultra-fine insulin needle, while others are available in oral or nasal formulations. Full step-by-step administration instructions and sterile supplies are provided at your visit. We do not publish dosing publicly.

f6.q: Will peptides replace my hormone replacement therapy?
f6.a: No. Peptides and bioidentical hormones operate via different signaling mechanisms. Peptides generally work far more effectively once underlying hormone, thyroid, and nutrient levels are already balanced.

f7.q: Are these considered performance enhancing drugs?
f7.a: Several growth hormone secretagogues and related peptides are prohibited by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and competitive athletic federations. If you participate in sanctioned competitive sports, please disclose this during your initial consultation.

f8.a: Results vary based on the specific protocol, baseline health, and accompanying foundational corrections. Most patients report measurable improvements within 90 days when combined with nutrition, sleep, and hormone optimization.
